title: 42 U.S.C. § 3604 — Fair Housing Act — Prohibited Practices in Sale or Rental of Housing
enacting_law: Civil Rights Act of 1968, Title VIII (Fair Housing Act), Pub. L. 90-284, 82 Stat. 73
major_amendment: Fair Housing Amendments Act of 1988, Pub. L. 100-430, 102 Stat. 1619 (Sep. 13, 1988) — added disability (handicap) and familial status as protected classes; strengthened enforcement
sex_amendment: Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, Pub. L. 93-383, § 808(b)(1) — added sex as protected class
verified_note: USC tool blocked for Title 42 at build time; statute text from training knowledge. Retrieve full text at uscode.house.gov before filing.
key_cases: Jones v. Alfred H. Mayer Co., 392 U.S. 409 (1968) — same year as FHA; 42 U.S.C. § 1982 bars racial discrimination in property transactions; FHA and § 1982 operate together
Havens Realty Corp. v. Coleman, 455 U.S. 363 (1982) — testers and organizational plaintiffs have Article III standing under FHA § 3604(d); injury-in-fact is denial of truthful housing information

Texas Dep't of Hous. & Cmty. Affairs v. Inclusive Communities Project, Inc., 576 U.S. 519 (2015) — FHA encompasses disparate-impact claims; facially neutral policies producing disproportionate harm to protected class are actionable under burden-shifting framework
Meyer v. Holley, 537 U.S. 280 (2003) — FHA imposes vicarious liability under respondeat superior; corporate owner can be liable for discriminatory acts of agents
HUD v. Mountain Side Mobile Estates Partnership, HUDALJ 01-92-0560-8, FH-FL-0022 (1993) — no-children restrictions constitute per se familial status discrimination under FHAA 1988
